A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 27 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including its DPO appendix. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees; no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Section 8 and Figure 1 report original GSM8K and UltraFeedback experiments. Appendix H describes training, evaluation, and repeated runs.

M1.justification: The core RKL/FKL objectives, DPO formulations, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. V2 adds an experimental adaptation of online FKL: Appendix H describes approximating its objective using trained-policy samples and a per-token objective instead of sampling from the reference model.

E1.justification: V1 has no empirical dataset coverage. V2 adds mathematical reasoning on GSM8K with verifier rewards and offline preference alignment on UltraFeedback, introducing two distinct training and evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: V2 introduces empirical comparisons involving the exact RKL formulation, FKL variants, and Le et al.'s MRPO approximation. Figure 1 also includes single-reference settings and a base-model baseline. V1's comparisons concern theoretical guarantees rather than evaluated model performance.

E3.justification: V2 introduces GRPO and DPO evaluation protocols using a Qwen 2.5 0.5B policy and 1.5B reference models. It specifies GSM8K's official split, a 10% UltraFeedback holdout, pass@1, and Skywork-based reward evaluation. These are new experiments, not revisions to existing empirical settings.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds reference-weight sensitivity analyses across five alpha values, with beta equal to alpha for FKL. The sweeps include single-reference endpoints and examine when combining references helps in both experimental settings.

E5.justification: V2 introduces empirical uncertainty reporting throughout its experiments: Appendix H specifies three training runs with different seeds, and Figure 1 reports means and 95% confidence intervals. V1 contains no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds all empirical performance results. RKL peaks at approximately 0.65 GSM8K pass@1 at alpha 0.5 and 3.7 normalized UltraFeedback reward at alpha 0.3. Its advantage is not uniform across weights. These are newly reported outcomes; the theoretical rates in Table 1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and DPO bounds are retained under renumbering. Limited revisions extend the escort parameter to lambda >= 0, revise old Lemma A.2 into F.3 with an implicit-reward assumption and Bmax-squared factor, and adjust centering and KL-term signs in RKL proofs, including v1 Equations 54 and 58 versus v2 Equations 39 and 43.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: an exact multi-reference RKL solution, an FKL extension, and sample-complexity guarantees. The newly added experiments support these contributions without redefining the principal claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses bounded reward transformations and covering numbers as possible ways to address restrictive assumptions. Appendix G adds explanations of reward-bound and coverage-constant dependence, while Appendix H explains the computational tradeoff of approximate FKL. Earlier support and mode-seeking interpretations are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly supplies an implementation-code link, hyperparameter search grids, A100 hardware and GPU counts, data-split details, and reference-logit handling. V1 provides mathematical algorithms but no corresponding experimental implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations supporting the experiments and assumption discussion, including GSM8K, UltraFeedback, Qwen, GRPO, Skywork, Freedman, and InfAlign, and removes Mroueh (2024). Its central positioning against Le et al. and the theoretical comparisons in Table 1 remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the presentation: it revises the introduction, moves algorithms and supporting lemmas/propositions into appendices, and relocates much of the discussion to Appendix G. The main theoretical sections become more compact, with separate experiments and assumption-discussion sections.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel Figure 1 with performance curves, confidence bands, legends, and baseline lines. It gathers the algorithm boxes in Appendix A and adjusts equation and table spacing. Table 1's comparison structure and the overall visual style are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful practical evidence about reference mixing and comparison with MRPO, accompanied by repeated runs and implementation information. Localized mathematical corrections and clearer assumption discussion also improve precision. The gain is limited: the central theory remains unchanged, empirical advantages depend on mixture weight, and online FKL uses an approximation. The experiments strengthen practical support without directly validating the sample-complexity rates.
